purpose: Orbital Rivals production card art and lobby cover

atlas.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production collectible sci-fi card-game illustration atlas for Orbital Rivals.
Create ONE SQUARE 2048x2048 image. It is an exact regular grid with FOUR equal-width COLUMNS and SEVEN equal-height ROWS, filling the entire square edge to edge: 28 separate painted landscape illustrations. Each cell is 1/4 image width by 1/7 image height. NO gutters, NO border lines, NO frames, NO labels, NO text, NO lettering, NO numbers. Abrupt clean scene boundaries at the exact grid divisions. The game will crop each exact cell, so never let a ship or an important shape cross into another cell. Keep each main subject centered and entirely inside its own cell with a little breathing room.
Every cell must look like actual rich hand-painted collectible-card art, not icons or diagrams: vivid dramatic science-fiction illustration, crisp chunky ship silhouettes, painterly hull metal and alien material texture, glowing engines, rim light, swirling nebulae, tiny stars and planets. Slightly playful stylized proportions, premium polished game art, highly legible at tiny card size. Each cell is a different scene, no repetition.
Columns left to right in EVERY row: (1) small utility/scout/courier spacecraft, (2) powerful combat capital spacecraft, (3) floating space station/base, (4) fortified armored orbital outpost.
Rows top to bottom:
ROW 1 neutral independent human fleet: cream and orange worn salvage-metal retro spacecraft, warm orange engine glows, deep blue space.
ROW 2 Trade Federation: cyan blue and white sleek clean spacecraft, shielded glass cockpits, cool blue nebula.
ROW 3 Blob: bright emerald green organic alien living spacecraft and biomorphic stations, tentacles, chitin, luminous eyes, green bioluminescence, no mechanical human hulls.
ROW 4 Star Empire: magenta and crimson angular imperial spacecraft, knife-shaped wings, red laser batteries, grand threatening red-purple nebula.
ROW 5 Machine Cult: lilac and steel gray robotic spacecraft and factory stations, articulated claw arms, mechanical cores, electric violet lights.
ROW 6 Solar Dominion: gold and ivory sun-wing spacecraft, radiant golden solar sails, sun temples and radiant orbital citadels, warm amber space.
ROW 7 Void Syndicate: dark violet crescent ships, black-purple curved hulls, mysterious bright lavender gravitational cores, ring-shaped stations and shielded shadow outposts, deep indigo space.
All 28 complete separate compositions must be visible. Exact 4 columns and 7 rows. No title or typography anywhere. Not a UI mockup; only the painted scene atlas.

cover.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production landscape game cover / lobby tile for the sci-fi deckbuilding game ORBITAL RIVALS.
Create one beautiful polished painted game-cover image, landscape 3:2 composition, ideally 1536x1024. A dramatic fleet duel in space: a large sleek cyan-and-white gunship on the left faces a radiant gold-and-ivory winged dreadnought on the right across a luminous turquoise-violet central nebula and tiny glowing stars. Their silhouettes and engines are beautifully rendered, dramatic rim lighting and hand-painted metallic hull textures, colorful stylized premium collectible-card-game illustration. A few smaller emerald organic alien ships and lilac machine ships add scale. At the lower edge, three richly illustrated sci-fi playing cards fan out subtly as an unmistakable deckbuilder cue, with painted ship artwork, tiny simple stat shapes, no readable small labels or numbers. Keep major subjects readable in a small lobby tile. Bold cinematic composition with generous safe space for a big readable title.
Text verbatim: "ORBITAL RIVALS". Place this exact title very prominently in two stacked lines in the upper central area, large stylish cream/gold sci-fi display lettering with dark navy shadow and excellent contrast, fully inside the safe margins, readable when thumbnail sized. No other words, no subtitle, no watermark, no brand logos. The tile should feel exciting, playful, strategic and finished. Actual painted cover artwork, not a screenshot or HTML interface.

note: The generated atlas has seven slightly different row heights. Use orbital-rivals-art-atlas.json pixel rectangles with a three-pixel inset to avoid adjacent-scene seams.
